key_insight: LIGHT shows that high-quality contact-aware HOI animations can be generated without explicit classifier-based or hand-crafted contact priors by letting guidance emerge from the diffusion denoising pace itself.
problem_solved: Generates realistic human-object interaction animations that jointly model dynamic human motions and diverse object geometries while avoiding brittle, manually designed contact priors or kinematic constraints.
method: Diffusion-forcing framework: modify the denoising process so the denoising pace itself provides emergent guidance toward plausible contact and interaction states.
Data-driven contact modeling: learn contact and interaction cues directly from data instead of injecting hand-crafted contact priors or external classifier guidance.
Joint human+object representation: generate temporally coherent human motion and object geometry together to improve interaction realism and contact fidelity.
impact: Makes HOI animation more robust and generalizable by removing dependence on manual priors or classifiers, simplifying deployment across diverse objects and actions while improving contact realism.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing input (pose + object), diffusion denoising steps, and emergent guidance loop leading to final animation
Before/after comparison frames highlighting contact quality with and without LIGHT
Illustration of denoising timeline (heatmap over timesteps) showing how guidance emerges across steps
Gallery of diverse HOI examples (different objects and actions) to demonstrate generalization
paper_title: Unleashing Guidance Without Classifiers for Human-Object Interaction Animation
paper_authors: Ziyin Wang, Sirui Xu, Chuan Guo, Bing Zhou, Jiangshan Gong
